lesson_title: From a Messy Pile to a Neat Project
hook_text: Neo's desk is covered in photocopies, photos and notes. How does a messy pile become a project?
clip_script: Upington. Neo brings everything he has found: an old photo of the first canal, notes from his grandfather's interview, a page about grape farming, a drawing of an old plough. First, sort it into piles: before the town, the early town, the town today. Then put it in time order on a timeline. Then make short notes in your own words, with the source next to each one. Messy pile, three piles, a timeline, neat notes. Now the project almost writes itself.
visual_style: Whiteboard desk with a messy pile of papers that flies into three labelled boxes, then lines up along a timeline arrow.
mood: Satisfying, like tidying a room and finding everything.
pacing: Show the mess, sort it, line it up in time, then show neat notes.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort your own project notes into groups.
